known_anti_patterns: verify_receipt returned {"valid": true} for BOTH B1 (receipt c50bec8e...) and B2 (receipt c7d4829e...) even though both declare the SAME previous_receipt (A, 2cc3d1a6...) -- a real fork constructed against the live ferroplan-mcp server, not a mock

verify_receipt's contract is recompute-payload-digest + recompute-receipt + check previous_receipt is present and well-formed hex; it never looks the predecessor up, so it structurally cannot see a sibling claiming the same parent

the only place 'fork' is mentioned anywhere in this repository outside CE-GALL-31/34's own text is agents/receipt-auditor.md, and that is a markdown prompt instructing an LLM to reject forked heads -- it is prose, not an invocable script or MCP tool, and was not exercised against B1/B2
grep -rn verify_chain crates/ plugins/ (excluding this checkpoint's own test/receipt) returns nothing, confirming CE-GALL-31's original finding still holds at this revision

negative_falsifier.why_this_counts: pins the exact live-tool outputs for two divergent plan-admission envelopes (B1, B2) that both declare the same previous_receipt as their predecessor (A). verify_receipt was called on each independently and both returned valid: true with no field indicating a sibling exists or that global chain uniqueness was checked. This IS the undetected fork: constructed for real against the running MCP server, not asserted from a comment, and silently accepted by every check this repository exposes

title: Receipt chain fork detection -- absent capability, demonstrated
